title: 35 MINUTES AGGRESSIVE MORNING PRAYER TO COMMAND THE DAY
text: The week has already started. Not for you, for the enemy. He did not wait for Monday morning. He did not take Sunday off. While you were resting, he was assembling. >> [music] >> While you were sleeping, he was strategizing. While you were in church singing, he was positioning [music] his forces for the 7 days you are about to walk into. He has already written a version of your week. He has already assigned spirits to your Monday, to your Tuesday, to your Wednesday. He has already [music] identified which doors he intends to close, which relationships he intends to [music] poison, which opportunities he intends to intercept, which discouragement he intends to deploy, which accident he has assigned to your road. He has a version of your week. The question is, are you going to let him run it? Or are you going to do what the scripture says? >> [music] >> What Job 38:12 says, "Has thou commanded the morning?" What the sons of Issachar understood, 1 Chronicles 12:32, "Men who had understanding of the times to know what Israel ought to do." What Daniel did, Daniel 6:10, he prayed three [music] times a day regardless of the decree. What David did, Psalm 5:3, "In the morning I will direct my prayer unto thee." You are going to command this week before it commands you. Before the enemy's version is released, before his assignments become operational, you are going to set the terms. >> [music] >> And that is exactly what the next 35 minutes are. Not devotional time, not gentle morning reflection, violent, aggressive, intentional, um, warfare. Matthew chapter 11:12, >> [music] >> "And from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force. The violent, >> [music] >> the ones who refuse to start a week without first taking it by force in prayer. >> [music] >> The ones who understand that the kingdom does not fall into passive hands. It is not too late to take the week by force, even on Tuesday, even on Wednesday. Send it now, [music] then come back. The war room is open. The theology of Monday morning. Before we pray, I want to give you the theology of Monday morning because you cannot pray aggressively over something you do not understand. You cannot command what you have not first comprehended. And when you understand what a week actually is in the spirit realm, you will never enter one [music] passively again. A week is a battle ground, not a calendar. In the natural realm, a week is 7 days, 168 hours, a unit [music] of time for scheduling and planning. But in the spirit realm, a week is a theater of war. It is the arena in which the kingdom of God and the kingdom of darkness contend for the outcomes of your life. Every day is a battlefield. Every hour is contested ground. The sharp axe requires less effort to accomplish more. Monday morning prayer is the sharpening of the axe. [music] The believer who prays aggressively on Monday morning enters the week with a sharp edge. The believer who does not spends all week exerting more effort for less result.
